question: When did the central office of the Reserve Bank of India shift to Mumbai?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1937**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was established on **1 April 1935**, in Kolkata under the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• The central office of the Reserve Bank of India was shifted from Kolkata to **Mumbai in 1937**.
 
• Mumbai became the permanent headquarters of the RBI, primarily due to its strategic location as the financial capital of India.
 
• As the central office, the Mumbai branch houses the Governor’s office and is responsible for policy formulation.
 
• The RBI was initially a privately-owned institution but was nationalized in **1949** after India's independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI):**

 
 
• It is India's central bank and the regulator of the financial system.
 
• The RBI controls the issue and supply of the Indian Rupee and manages foreign exchange under the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.
 
• It plays a crucial role in monetary policy formulation to ensure price stability and economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Governance Structure:**
 
 
• The RBI is governed by a central board of directors, which includes the Governor, Deputy Governors, and other appointed members.
 
• The Governor is the chief executive officer of the RBI and is appointed by the Government of India.
 
 
 
• **Functions of the RBI:**
 
 
• Formulates and implements monetary policy to maintain inflation and economic stability.
 
• Supervises and regulates banks and financial institutions to ensure financial stability.
 
• Acts as a banker to the government and manages public debt.
 
• Manages foreign exchange and controls the currency supply in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The RBI was modeled on the lines of the Bank of England and initially functioned as a privately-owned bank.
 
• After nationalization in 1949, it became a fully government-owned institution.
 
• The RBI has played a pivotal role in shaping India's economic policies, especially post-independence.
